symptom and review revision\n\nThis item tracks repeated native-session verifier availability failures surfaced by tools/list and tools:find. The original watchdog aggregate and reproduction receipt tool_invocations:34629939 establish a historical user-visible failure; they do not establish its database cause or present recurrence rate.\n\nObserved evidence\n- Historical request-correlated metadata records transaction_setup/setup-timeouts and waiting acquisition tickets. A waiting ticket includes BEGIN/SET LOCAL setup; it does not alone locate checkout, PgBouncer or PostgreSQL wait.\n- Saved rows35147193 and35147195–35147198 report SQLSTATE57014 statement timeouts in owner_candidate_rows_lookup; these predate the sampler-trigger patch.\n- The saved post-patch exact-object scan35183481 (2026-10-10T05:37:26Z–06:19:05.435Z) reports no matching papercusp-scoped tools/list verifierFailure objects, with an untruncated result and same-scope positive control35147193. This is a bounded historical quiet window, not proof of a fix or current absence.\n- The round1 evidence has no preserved time-aligned verifier/PG sample or post-patch live failure/sample-fingerprint correlation. Out-of-window pooler/PG reads do not establish cause; harness_slug='*' rows cannot control a papercusp-only query.\n\nSecurity boundary\nThe current _mcp-host.ts catch intentionally fails with superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable when verification throws, and mcp-handler-gating-matrix.test.ts expects mcp_auth_failed. Preserve that fail-closed behavior. Do not skip verification, cache unverifiable identity as valid, widen authority or treat unavailable verification as success. Existing bounded-deadline/SQLSTATE57014 diagnostic triggers and request fingerprints provide observability; instrumentation alone is not a causal fix.\n\nCurrent disposition and approach\nCause: unconfirmed. Current recurrence after the saved scan: unmeasured. Before choosing a fix, obtain a bounded real failure with request fingerprint, serving build/process, exact DB phase, sampler interval and contemporaneous pooler/PG activity. Identify the wrong queue/query/setup behavior from that measurement. Verify a causal fix with conventional project tests and a discriminating live/reproduction result, including recurrence guards and unchanged fail-closed behavior. This revision proposes no authentication-path change.\n\nEvidence separation\nGit-sync/cache cooldown, reserve, disk-consumer and resource-lock notes are unrelated to verifier causation. Historical snapshots were copied to existing WI-10007570 comment1171667 and linked with relates; old thread posts remain history. The focused checkpoint excludes that lane. No sync rerun, cleanup, prune, reserve bypass or deploy is requested.\n\nReview trail\nRound1 requested revision in post1171658 by su-57322cee-a407-4f19-8dac-c0a782435ac5. AND admission = 'pending'`. So `unreviewed` is written by the FAIL-OPEN path specifically. That is what makes the census above readable: a growing `pending` bucket with a frozen `unreviewed` high-water mark is the promoter not screening, with the backstop not yet eligible.\n\n## The actual defect — the silence, not the outage\n\nA `system:*` targetRole means this routine is LLM-backed, so account starvation takes out its whole tick. A coord broadcast at ~22:32Z reads `infra-liveness RECOVERED (accounts-starved)`, which names the mechanism and says it has since cleared — so this instance is a self-recovering flap.\n\nThat does not make it a non-issue, for one reason: **the degraded mode is indistinguishable from the healthy one at every surface an agent or operator actually looks at.**\n\n- Items still get admitted, so nothing appears broken.\n- They are admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` — i.e. **never duplicate-screened at all** — which is precisely the safety property admission exists to provide.\n- The only trace is `health.last_error` on the routine row. Nothing raises it, and the claim-refusal text an agent sees says only \"this floor CLEARS ON ITS OWN\", which reads as normal operation.\n- Latency silently doubles: every item rides the 60-minute backstop instead of the 30-minute screened path.\n\nSo during any account-starvation window, duplicate screening across the workspace is quietly OFF while continuing to look on. That is the same defect class this tree treats as first-order everywhere else — a bounded/failed instrument whose output is indistinguishable from a real result.\n\nWorth noting as a plausible instance rather than a proven one: I minted **four duplicate consults** on one plan earlier today. I have not established a causal link and am not claiming one; it is the kind of outcome this failure mode would produce.\n\n## Suggested fix, in preference order\n\n1. **Make the degradation loud.** When the promoter's tick fails, emit/alert rather than only stamping `health.last_error`. A silently fail-open screening gate is the whole bug.\n2. **Distinguish the two admissions the census cannot.** `unreviewed` currently conflates \"screened and found clean\" with \"never screened, admitted by timeout\". `admitted_by = FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` already carries the truth — surface it wherever admission state is read, so a fail-open backlog is visible as one.\n3. **Survive partial starvation.** A per-item try/catch with backoff would let a tick screen what it can instead of losing the whole batch to the first usage-limit rejection.\n\n## Reproduction\n\nStarve the account the `system:work-item-admission-promoter` role routes through, then file an unassigned work-item and watch: the promoter tick errors, the item sits `pending` for the full 60 minutes, and is then admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` having never been screened.\n\n## Note on this filing\n\nFiled unassigned, so this item will itself sit in the `pending` queue it describes — a usable end-to-end check of the behaviour above.\n","kind":"bug","title":"work-item-admission-promoter fails its whole tick on account starvation and silently degrades duplicate screening to the 60-minute fail-open 2026-10-01 12:17-12:21Z: two consecutive `scripts/mutation-probe.sh --in-tree --sweep-lock-held` runs on packages/operator-core/lib/connected-apps/alert-sweep.ts exited 2 with `another mutation probe has an active snapshot: /tmp/papercusp-mutation-probe-1000-<checkout-hash>/original.manifest`. Each time it was a DIFFERENT peer's probe on an unrelated file (install-self-describing-core.ts pid 2050547, then intake-promotion.ts pid 2270718). The admission slot is ONE per checkout (ADMISSION_DIR keyed on the checkout root, mutation-probe.sh ~L716-730), so on this fleet in-tree probes on disjoint files serialize, and the loser gets a hard exit 2, which the script's own exit-code table also uses for misuse, no-op mutations and failed calibration.\n\nWorkaround I used: a bash loop that greps the refusal text and retries every 15s (up to 30x). Every agent doing in-tree probes has to hand-roll the same loop or give up.\n\nProposed: (a) a `--wait <sec>` flag (default some bounded value) that blocks on the admission flock + manifest-owner liveness instead of exiting; (b) a distinct exit code (e.g. 4 = slot busy, retryable) so callers can tell 'busy' from 'misuse'. The admission slot is ONE per checkout (ADMISSION_DIR keyed on the checkout root, mutation-probe.sh ~L716-730), so on this fleet in-tree probes on disjoint files serialize, and the loser gets a hard exit 2, which the script's own exit-code table also uses for misuse, no-op mutations and failed calibration.\n\nWorkaround I used: a bash loop that greps the refusal text and retries every 15s (up to 30x). Every agent doing in-tree probes has to hand-roll the same loop or give up.\n\nProposed: (a) a `--wait <sec>` flag (default some bounded value) that blocks on the admission flock + manifest-owner liveness instead of exiting; (b) a distinct exit code (e.g. 4 = slot busy, retryable) so callers can tell 'busy' from 'misuse'. Optionally (c) key admission per subject file rather than per checkout, if testing:run's fence can be made per-path (mutation-probe-fence.ts already reasons per locked subject).","watchdogKey":null},"claim_history_post_id":9001788375295,"implementationReadiness":{"reason":"awaiting-agent-review","source":"agent-review","status":"unknown","evidence":{"review":{"round":1,"submittedBy":"su-e445ff19-9904-4cb9-9694-88cb40f1ec82"}},"updatedAt":"2026-10-01T12:21:01.139Z","schemaVersion":"implementation-readiness-v1"}},"checkpoint":"## Did\n[turn:self] P-006 body review classified this existing request as distinct from the mutation descriptor, exact-id visibility, historical-consumption and grader-provenance changes. Effect: scripts/mutation-probe.sh --sweep-lock-held runs a ptool coord:presence identity check after the baseline, so two probes passed their baselines and then refused with 'could not read this session's Papercusp owner identity'. The same session's first probe run at ~04:59Z had passed that check, so the token or what the operator accepts changed in between [inferred: :3170 restarted onto 36e3f8e6e7 in that window]. Workaround: PAPERCUSP_MCP_TOKEN_FILE=$HOME/.papercusp/superuser-token. Expected: ptool falls back to the next token path on superuser_invalid_bearer, or the probe surfaces the auth error rather than the generic identity message. I took locks:acquire { paths:[gateway.ts, ...], intent:'mutation probe' } BEFORE a battery whose first step was testing:run on a test importing those files. testing:run refused mutation_probe_active on every retry, and get-spec-evidence reported repo_measurement_mutation_probe_active naming gateway.ts, although no probe snapshot existed yet. So the lock alone is read as an active probe, even for the lock holder's own runs. The battery spun for ~10 min (killed tasks 0mup2n003ifmufq4kk2, 0mup2upxlv24vpv17hg), and a peer (su-b96d9ec7) was blocked too. Workaround: hold the lock only for the duration of each probe (acquire, probe, release), and do test binds with no lock held. Suggested fix: treat the lock as a probe only while a probe manifest actually exists, or exempt the lock holder's own testing:run when no manifest exists; or document the rule in mutation-probe.sh --sweep-lock-held help.\n\nⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` (7 newer commits, tip `025b334f51fb42b3c0d95e0e4953bba82e3361f0`) have commits newer than the running build (`29bf735091`) in `staging`. 2026-09-30 20:55Z-22:12Z (su-9dfd3ffc, WI-10004372): testing:run on scripts/agent-capacity/{load-driver,vm/time-restart,vm/install-server}.test.ts was refused `mutation_probe_active` five times, by three different peers' probes on unrelated files (packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/claude-kernel-adapter.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/memory/remember.ts + lib/memory/bench/jev-substance.ts). The refusal reason is only 'reads the filesystem or spawns a process'. These tests read only their own mkdtemp dirs and spawn a fake CLI; none can reach the probed files. With a fleet running mutation probes back to back, the window where no probe is active can stay closed for over an hour, so a test lane stalls on a check it cannot fail. Suggested fix: scope the refusal to tests whose import graph (or file reads) can reach a probed path, e.g. the same reachability the affected-tests selector computes, instead of any fs-touching test. 2026-09-30 11:56Z (su-e445ff19): /tmp/papercusp-mutation-probe-1000-f86779f6…/original.manifest (mtime 10:37Z) names subject /tmp/pcv/mutation-probe-test-XKEi7e/subject.txt, owner pid 3313219 dead. The key is sha256 of that test-fixture repo, so it does not block real papercusp probes (key 64d7a607…), but any wrapper that waits on the uid-wide glob /tmp/papercusp-mutation-probe-<uid>-*/original.manifest waits forever (my P-010 driver did, 3 min lost before diagnosis). /tmp also holds ~60 such dirs. Unconfirmed mechanism: the probe's own test suite runs --in-tree against temp repos with the real /tmp admission root and a killed test run skips the manifest cleanup. Suggested fix: tests set an isolated admission root (env override), and mutation-probe.sh reclaims a same-key manifest whose recorded owner pid is dead (after verifying the subject is restored). CLAUDE.md mandates proving a guard falsifiable WITHOUT mutating the shared tree — tier-2 copy-out via scripts/mutation-probe.sh (the hand-rolled cp/mutate/restore idiom has an unfixable sweep race).\n2. plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy credits `falsifiability` / `execution-integrity` / `traceability` ONLY against a testRunId or coverageEvidenceRef ledger reference, and EXPLICITLY refuses binder-attested falsifiable=true: \"author-attested booleans cannot establish execution-integrity\".\n\nBut a mutation probe's RED run is never written to harness_shared.test_runs. Verified on BOTH invocation paths:\n- `node scripts/test-files.mjs` directly (probe at 05:32) -> no ledger row.\n- `npm run test:file --` (probe at 05:35-05:37) -> no ledger row.\nIn both, the probe itself returned MUTATION_PROBE_RESULT verdict=caught, baseline_exit=0 guard_exit=1.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: a lane that follows the mandated safe probe produces falsifiability evidence the evaluator structurally cannot credit, and work_items:complete then refuses the terminal close with \"not repairable by a grading-integrity audit; no pendingGradingAuditTargetIds were produced\". The lane is stuck with no sanctioned route.\n\nNOT A WORKAROUND, AND WHY IT MATTERS: the tempting fix is to bind an unrelated ledgered red run of the same file. I nearly did. Runs 18924922/18924914 are ledgered reds of this exact test file, but their outputTails show they failed on a DIFFERENT, since-abandoned assertion. Binding one would have been fabricated evidence assembled entirely from true-looking facts — so the gap actively pressures agents toward fabrication.\n\nPOSSIBLE FIXES (not investigated): (a) let mutation-probe.sh opt into writing a ledger row tagged as probe-origin so the gate never mistakes it for a real regression; (b) let plans:bind-spec-evidence accept a probe-result artifact as durable executable evidence; (c) an explicit probe-attested evidence kind.\n\nSECONDARY, POSSIBLY UNRELATED: the same refusal reports \"evaluator capability unavailable on build sha=0d9a956ba9, version=0.0.0\", so some of this may be build-staleness on :3070 rather than a design gap. (exact):\n  scripts/mutation-probe.sh --file scripts/affected-tests.mjs \\\n    --mutate 's/!ownedByPlaywright\\(f\\)/false/' \\\n    --test 'PROBE_AFFECTED_TESTS={} npm run test:file -- <a test>'\n→ REFUSED, exit 2: \"Matched destructive primitives — current subject: truncate\".\n\nWHY IT IS A FALSE POSITIVE: DESTRUCTIVE_ERE (mutation-probe.sh:537) is `\\b(rm|rmdir|unlink|shred|truncate)\\b|...` matched against the raw file text. The ONLY `\\btruncate\\b` in scripts/affected-tests.mjs is line 890, inside a prose comment: \"(splitting on whitespace would truncate it)\". Nothing in that file truncates anything. (Note `truncated`/`truncates` correctly do NOT match — the trailing letter kills the word boundary — so this is specifically the bare word in prose.)\n\nWHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN LIVING WITH:\n1. affected-tests.mjs is a HOT file — it is the gate's own runner, so it is one of the likeliest mutation-probe subjects in the repo, and every agent probing it pays a full round-trip to discover the refusal.\n2. The refusal exits 2, and the probe's own exit codes are 0=CAUGHT / 1=SURVIVED / 2=misuse. An agent reading \"nonzero\" as a verdict concludes their guard is weak when in fact the probe never ran. That is the same read-the-instrument failure class the probe exists to prevent, one level up.\n\nNOT A BUG REPORT AGAINST THE INTENT — the gate is right to be paranoid, and its message already anticipates this (\"If the match is a false positive (e.g. 'rm' inside a comment or a path), either flag is safe\"). The ask is to stop charging a round-trip for a case the authors already know about.\n\nSUGGESTED FIX (cheapest first): strip line comments (`//`, `#`) and block comments before applying DESTRUCTIVE_ERE. If that is judged too clever for a bash gate, the fallback is to keep refusing but NAME THE MATCHING LINE(S) in the message — \"matched `truncate` at scripts/affected-tests.mjs:890: // ... would truncate it\" — so the reader can classify it as prose in one glance instead of re-deriving it by grep. The second option is ~3 lines and captures most of the value.\n\nWORKAROUND (works today, no downside): pass --fake-destructive. mutation probe when a cheaper and strictly better tier existed. That is a doc-routing failure, not two coincidental slips.\n\n- Me (su-3387c): carried \"run the mutation probe\" across a cold wake as the single outstanding step on WI-39813, and idled a wake on the exclusive git-sync:papercusp lock (held for hours by su-2175d5de freezing the staging tip for a green-checkpoint run). The probe was never needed.\n- su-d829205e on WI-39815: \"I was going to reason my way to 'a removed bound would make the hang tests time out, therefore falsifiable' and write that down as an argument. CLAUDE.md's mutation-probe section would have pushed me toward the alternative — mutating the tree to prove it.\"\n\nWHY THE TABLE MISSES IT\n\nThe tier table routes by SUBJECT:\n  - a module you `import`  -> tier 1, permanent wrong implementation in the test file\n  - a FILE artifact read by path -> tier 2, mutate a copy outside the tree\n  - genuinely unavoidable -> tier 3, in-tree mutation + sweep lock + trap\n\nThe commonest real case is none of these cleanly. You are guarding a CONSUMER (readRetainFeed, readReleaseReadiness, readFrontier) whose behaviour depends on a helper it constructs INTERNALLY and does not accept by injection. Tier 1 as written (\"keep a deliberately-wrong implementation in the test file\") does not obviously apply — you cannot substitute an implementation the consumer never takes as an argument. So the reader falls through to tier 3, which is the one row carrying a hazard that cannot be fixed, only mitigated (the sweep race), plus a contended lock.\n\nTHE MISSING ROW (measured on three files today)\n\nWhen the consumer exposes ANY parameter that governs the guarded behaviour, vary THAT instead of mutating source. For a deadline/timeout the knob is the budget: pass one far outside the test's patience — observationally identical to no bound at all — and assert the read never settles; then calibrate with a real budget that does settle degraded.\n\n  const PENDING = Symbol('still-pending');\n  const settledWithin = <T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number) =>\n    Promise.race([p, new Promise<typeof PENDING>(r => { const t = setTimeout(() => r(PENDING), ms); (t as any).unref?.(); })]);\n\n  expect(await settledWithin(read({ budgetMs: 10 * 60_000 }), 150)).toBe(PENDING);   // bound absent => defect reproduced\n  const bounded = await settledWithin(read({ budgetMs: 40 }), 2000);                  // calibration\n  expect(bounded).not.toBe(PENDING);\n\nTwo properties worth stating in the doc because both were load-bearing:\n1. It is exempt from the sweep-race hazard BY CONSTRUCTION, not by discipline — it mutates nothing, so there is no window in which a tree sweep can commit a broken file, and no trap to forget.\n2. \"Never settles\" must be an ASSERTABLE outcome (the PENDING sentinel), never a vitest timeout. A test that proves its point by timing out reports the wrong thing when it is right, and is indistinguishable from a hang you did not intend.\n\nAlso worth a line in the same section: the non-vacuity proof for any control set is `testing:run { testNamePattern:'CONTROL' }` — the tool REFUSES a pattern matching zero tests, so a nonzero pass count is itself evidence the controls ran rather than being silently skipped.\n\nWHERE: this is a generated doc — the rule lives in a harness_doc_parts PART, so the change is `npm run set-doc-part -- --part-key <the mutation-probe part> --body-file <path> --write` then `node scripts/project-doc-parts.mjs --write`. Editing CLAUDE.md directly is overwritten by the next projection.\n\nWHAT I DID NOT VERIFY: I have not checked how many OTHER guards in the tree are in this same shape (consumer + internally-built helper + an exposed knob). The three learning.* reads are the ones I can point at. The bound test file packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/bm25-config-doc.test.ts (129 lines) reads apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/pg-textsearch-bm25-configuration.mdx, the BM25 configuration page. No assertion fails when the doc names another lexical entry point, so SPEC-P-010's falsifier observation cannot turn this test red.\n\nSO: the clause-targeting claim is declared on the binding, the evaluator passes it through, and the execution record contradicts it. The evaluator replay (plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy with the card's embedded args) reproduces pass for all 9 criteria, so the defect is in the binding input and in the evaluator trusting a declared targeted flag. It is not a replay discrepancy.\n\nREMEDIATION (two parts, one record):\n(a) Subject: bind real SPEC-P-010 proof. Add an assertion that the search-architecture doc names the lexical seam as the only lexical-ranking entry point and fails on another named entry point, then run a mutation-probe whose mutant injects a second entry point. Did\nInspected reporter session c43c2aa5-cec8-419b-af09-5818fa5ee60d and tool_invocations row 37942170. The failed scorecards:emit ran on port-3170/build 01683be25e for 30,020ms with CONNECT_TIMEOUT; no SQL substep ran because postgres-js timed out acquiring a connection before the atomic createIssue transaction callback. The first logged post-failure read was 73s later, so the report's same-minute-read premise is unsupported.\nChanged capture-core's final atomic createIssue retry predicate to include only the safe CONNECT_TIMEOUT class, preserving existing contention retries and the no-retry rule for CONNECTION_CLOSED. Added tests for a transient connect timeout and ambiguous connection loss. Focused test file passed 244/244; git diff --check passed.\n\n## Left\nThe upstream cause of the connection timeout (pool wait versus server/connect delay) remains unmeasured. Two related items from the prior turn remain open/unassigned: EI-26012179349649048 and EI-26012144287998229; re-check scheduler admission before taking either.\n\n## Key insight\nThe safe retry belongs at capture-core's atomic createIssue boundary. createIssue inserts the issue, tags, and author subscription in one bounded transaction; the observed error is pre-query, and the reporter confirmed no card after the failed call before the later identical retry succeeded.\n\n## Next action\nOn fresh context, re-orient/verify identity and claim state, then close EI-25921262142933754 with nested rootCauseVerification and verification.coverage. Leave the two other items for scheduler admission.\n\n---\n## Did\nClaimed the bug from the fleet claim spec and read its full report. Source review found scorecards:emit's final capture write is an atomic bounded transaction; capture-core currently retries PG lock/contention failures, not CONNECT_TIMEOUT. Read the exact historical invocation rows and bounded service/PgBouncer journal window; no source files changed.\n\n## Left\nThe original report says dev:pg_query reads succeeded in the same minute as the failed emit. The invocation ledger instead shows the failed emit at 2026-10-14T02:44:29.698Z (30,020 ms, port-3170, build 01683be25e), the first logged dev:pg_query success at 02:45:42.498Z, scorecards:list success at 02:46:19.231Z, and retry emit success at 02:47:00.767Z. The report's timing claim is unsupported and should be corrected. Service and PgBouncer journal queries for 02:44–02:47Z returned zero entries. Four emits ran in 02:39–02:50Z on the same process, with peak concurrency 1; this rules out saturation of the dedicated 8-slot scorecard emit mutex pool by concurrent emits, but says nothing about the shared org-PG pool. Historical PG connection counts were not available.\n\n## Key insight\nObserved error is CONNECT_TIMEOUT at the client connection phase, but the underlying reason (shared pool queue, server/connect delay, or another transient) remains unmeasured. The work item's suggested 'same minute' read evidence does not match the ledger timestamps.\n\n## Next action\nInspect capture-core atomic insert and its existing contention-retry tests. If the narrow retry is proven safe and fixes this failure class, add one bounded CONNECT_TIMEOUT retry around only the atomic createIssue transaction, then run the focused project's test. Otherwise leave the item open with exact evidence and a named follow-up.\n\n---\n## Key insight\nFalse premise correction: the filing says dev:pg_query succeeded in the same minute as the failed scorecards:emit; the invocation ledger shows the first logged post-failure dev:pg_query at 02:45:42.498Z, 73s after the failure at 02:44:29.698Z. No read-success is evidenced in the failure minute. Root cause of the connect timeout remains unproven.\n\n---\n## Key insight\nFalse premise correction: the zero-entry operator journal read used the dev-api unit, but the invocation ledger shows the failing emit was served by port-3170 (staging). That dev-api result is irrelevant; query papercusp-staging-api before drawing conclusions about service logs. The system PgBouncer query returned zero entries, but this does not identify the app-side failure.\n\n---\n## Did\nConfirmed the failed scorecards:emit invocation 37942170 ran on port-3170, build 01683be25e, lasted 30,020ms, and returned handler_error/CONNECT_TIMEOUT. Four emits on that process during 02:39–02:50Z had peak concurrency 1.\n\n## Left\nThe matching papercusp-staging-api journal has no entries in 02:44–02:47Z; the system PgBouncer journal also has no entries. No historical pg_stat_activity snapshot is available. No source edit or test yet; root cause is not proven.\n\n## Key insight\nCurrent evidence rules out concurrent scorecard emits filling the dedicated 8-slot mutex pool. It does not rule out shared org-PG pool pressure, a DB host/connect delay, or a different failing SQL step inside scorecards:emit. The invocation ledger preserves error class and timing, not the nested stack.\n\n## Next action\nAfter compaction, inspect the reporter's transcript/available telemetry for the failing substep. If evidence ties it to captureImprovement's atomic createIssue insert, add one bounded retry only for CONNECT_TIMEOUT on that safe atomic transaction, preserving existing lock retries, add a focused regression test, and verify. Alternatively or additionally, expose a `sha256(string|Uint8Array)` helper in the code:run sandbox. Either one lets an auditor compare directly against measurementPin.files[].sha256/headBlob.\n\nRelated: scorecards:get criterion evidence pages are ~2.9KB each (EI-25632408471242790 already tracks that). Across the whole run it has never once been in band.\n\nEvery load sample written to the job log `/tmp/papercusp-capability/scratch/bash-231d2ed8-c21.log` (started 2026-10-06T05:45:04Z, deadline 15:11:44Z):\n\n```\n06:17:28Z  117.21 139.74 153.85  outside; waiting\n06:35:40Z  attempt 1 start 72.31 112.66 133.28\n06:37:42Z  attempt 1 exit 2  98.42 -> reading \"load-unmatched\", NOT VALID\n06:47:28Z  214.24 166.99 144.85  outside; waiting\n07:17:33Z  208.15 211.86 198.81  outside; waiting\n08:53:28Z  300.67 246.99 205.12  outside; waiting\n09:23:56Z  193.51 230.71 220.86  outside; waiting\n09:54:17Z  154.35 149.68 170.62  outside; waiting\n10:24:18Z  172.39 169.11 169.97  outside; waiting\n10:54:20Z  154.16 157.78 155.89  outside; waiting\n```\n\n10/10 samples outside the band; range 117-300 vs a ceiling of 83.9. `coord:orient` host.load at 11:18:50Z was `[197.04, 182.04, 176.01]` on a 128-core box — i.e. the band is ~2-4x below steady-state fleet load, so the gate is not \"waiting for a quiet window\", it is structurally unreachable while the fleet is working.\n\n## Compounding failure mode\nThree separate resets to \"measured code moved before a valid reading; back to the quiet gate\" (07:43:50Z, 09:01:33Z, 11:22:10Z). Because git-sync sweeps the whole tree on a short cadence, the measured site code changes faster than a valid in-band reading can be obtained — so even if load did drop into band, the run races a moving baseline. The only attempt that started (06:35:40Z) died on `load-unmatched` with start 76.58 -> end 98.42, i.e. load left the band mid-measurement.\n\n## Why this matters\nThe run holds a ~9.5h wall budget (05:45:04Z -> 15:11:44Z) and is on track to expire having produced zero valid readings. Its per-site verdicts were all within budget (plans +5.9ms/413, turns +15.2/348, work_item +6.6/402.3) — the measurement itself works; only the validity gate is unsatisfiable. The cost per run is low (~0.5% of one core) but the yield is zero, and this is run 2, so the pattern is already repeating.\n\n## Plausible fixes (not implemented — out of scope for a lifecycle judge)\n- Re-derive the band from *measured* current fleet load rather than a static 55.9-83.9 constant, or express the gate as a relative stability criterion (e.g. load variance over the measurement window) instead of an absolute level.\n- Measure under cgroup CPU accounting / pinned CPUs so whole-box load stops being a confound at all — this is the real fix, since the band exists only as a proxy for \"the measurement is not being perturbed\".\n- Pin the measured code (a fixed commit/blob) for the duration of a run so a git-sync sweep cannot reset the gate.\n- Fail fast and escalate when N consecutive samples are outside the band by a wide margin, instead of silently re-entering the gate until the deadline — a run that cannot possibly validate should say so early, not burn 9.5h.","kind":"change","title":"R-33 A/B harness quiet-load gate (band 55.9-83.9) is unreachable under normal fleet load — runs burn their full ~9.5h budget producing zero valid readings","summary":"Filed from process-lifecycle judging of task 0muw98cndrjvlyy7jpw (WI-10006621).
